Define an endpoint

Source: R/Endpoint.R
Endpoint.Rd

Defines a binary or time-to-event endpoint by the columns of a patient-level data frame that hold it and by the direction in which it is favorable. The definitions are used by BenefitRisk, WinStat and SimSelection; any number of endpoints can be defined.

Usage

Endpoint(
  name,
  type = c("binary", "tte"),
  var = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  higher.better = TRUE
)

Arguments

name

Name of the endpoint, used to refer to it in the criteria of BenefitRisk and in the priority order of WinStat.

type

"binary" or "tte" (time to event).

var

For a binary endpoint, the name of the column with the values.

time, event

For a time-to-event endpoint, the names of the columns with the observed times and the event indicators.

higher.better

Logical: TRUE if a value of 1 (binary) or a longer time (time to event) is favorable.

Value

An object of class Endpoint: a list with elements name, type, var, time, event and higher.better.

Details

A binary endpoint is a column with values 0, 1 or NA, for example the objective response (higher.better = TRUE) or the occurrence of an adverse event (higher.better = FALSE). Missing values are excluded from the posterior distribution in BenefitRisk and make a pair uninformative for this endpoint in WinStat.

A time-to-event endpoint is given by a column of observed times and a column of event indicators (1 for an event, 0 for censoring), for example overall survival or progression-free survival. With higher.better = TRUE (the usual case) longer times are favorable.

See also

BenefitRisk, WinStat

Examples

eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
  Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE)
)
eps[[4]]$higher.better
#> [1] FALSE
